sentences.text: HON'BLE
MRS JUSTICE K.S. HEMALEKHA  ORAL ORDER

The petitioners are seeking for the following prayers:
"WHEREFORE, the Petitioners pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased declare that the proceedings under the provisions of Urban Lands Ceiling and Regulation Act 1976 stood lapsed as the possession of the schedule lands has not been taken over till 22-03-1999, when the Urban Land Ceiling and Regulations Act 1999 came into force in the interest of justice.
2. The Petitioners pray for a Writ of Prohibition directing the Respondents not to dispossess the Petitioners from the schedule lands in Sy.No.19/2 of Banasawadi Village, at Annexure-A No.ULC (9)
273/85-86, dated 02/12/1987 as the possession of the schedule lands has not been taken over by the Competent Authority under the Provisions of Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act 1976 in the interest of justice.

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: STATUTE

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
3. The Petitioners have pray for a direction to the Respondent No.3 Tahasildar to delete the name of the 2nd Respondent from column No.11 of the RTC extract and to enter the name of the NC:
2024:KHC:32963 Petitioners in column No.11 and 12 of the RTC in Annexure-D in the interest of justice.
4.

Therefore, the Petitioners respectfully pray that this Hon'ble court may be pleased to pass an appropriate order or direction as the case may be in the facts of the case as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in the circumstances in the interest of justice and equity."
2.

Heard Sri M.N. Uma Shankar, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Radha Ramaswamy,
learned Additional Government Advocate for the respondents.

3. The material on record would indicate that the petitioners have purchased the portion of the schedule lands in Sy. No.19/2 of Banasavadi Village measuring 2 acres 19 guntas (hereinafter Sri M Dhananjaya Reddy vs State Of Karnataka on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123431616/
3 referred to as 'schedule property' for short) under three registered sale deeds dated 14.02.2008,
11.02.2009 and 14.02.2008, the schedule property was acquired by Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) for formation of layout called scheme between Banasavadi Road and Hennur Road NC: 2024:KHC:32963 sanctioned by the BDA as per the notifications dated 21.03.1977 and 13.02.1989, the petitioners along with C. Balakrishna Reddy filed writ petition before this Court in W.P. No.38584/2016 seeking to declare that the acquisition proceedings insofar as it relates to Sy.
No.19/2 of Banaswadi Village are deemed to have lapsed in terms of Section 24 (2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 2013, as the physical possession of the lands has not been taken over or the compensation has not been paid to the petitioners, after issuance of notifications dated 21.03.1977 and 13.02.1989, the writ petition came to be allowed on 15.06.2021 and the impugned preliminary notification and final notification and all the acquisitions proceeding pursuant thereto have been quashed.
4.

sentences.text:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioners are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the schedule property having purchased from the lawful owners and recently the petitioners had noticed the proceedings under Sub-Section 1 of Section 10 of Urban NC: 2024:KHC:32963 Land (Ceiling Regulation) Act, 1976 was initiated and that the petitioners are entitled for benefit of the Urban Land (Ceiling Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999 (15 of 1999) as the possession of the schedule property has not been taken over till coming into force of the Repeal Act No.15 of 1999 with effect from 18.03.1999.
5.

entities.text: Urban Land (Ceiling Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999 (15 of 1999)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners that by virtue of Repealing of ULC Act,
with effect from 18.03.1999, the entire proceedings stand abated.

The Apex Court in the case of State of Uttar Pradesh Vs. Hari Ram1 (Hari Ram) has held that mere vesting of the land under Sub-Section 3 of Section 10 would not confer any right, on the State Government to have de facto possession of the vacant land unless there has been a voluntary surrender of vacant land before 18.03.1999, the State Government has to establish that there has been voluntary surrender of vacant land or surrender and delivery of peaceful possession under Sub- (2013) 4 SCC 280 NC:
2024:KHC:32963 Section 5 of Section 10 or forceful dispossession under Sub-Section 6 of Section 10.

entities.text: State of Uttar Pradesh Vs. Hari Ram1 (Hari Ram)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On failure to establish any of the situations, the land owner or holder can claim the benefit of Section 4 of the Repeal Act.

6. The Additional Government Advocate has filed a memo along with pahani for the year 2024-2025 pertaining to the schedule property indicating that in column No.9, the name of the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) has been entered as the land has been acquired by the BDA.

This Court in W.P. No.38584/2016 has already quashed the acquisition proceedings in respect of the schedule property, there are no materials are forthcoming to show that the respondents have taken over the possession of the schedule property and the possession continued to remain with the petitioner and the respondents having not taken over the possession of the schedule property from the petitioner, the impugned order needs to be quashed.

sentences.text: A careful perusal of the material on record would indicate that the possession of the schedule property has not been taken over by the respondents and in light of the decision of the Apex Court in the case of Hari Ram and by virtue of repeal of ULC Act, all the proceedings under the provisions of the ULC Act, 1976 stood lapsed, as the possession of the schedule property were not taken over on or before 18.03.1999, when the Repeal Act, 1999 came into force.

In the result, this Court pass the following:
ORDER (i) Writ petition is allowed.

(ii) The proceedings under the provisions of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation)
Act, 1976 stood lapsed as the possession of the suit property having not been taken over as on 18.03.1999, when the Repeal Act came into force.

(iii) Respondent No.3 to delete the name of respondent No.2 from Column No.11 of the RTC extract and enter the name of the petitioners in respect of NC:
2024:KHC:32963 revenue records as per the sale deeds, within three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

Sd/-
(K.S. HEMALEKHA) JUDGE S*
